correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian Fourier formula gives I=2exp(-S)(cosh Q+cos H). Taylor expansion gives M=S+H²/4 and T=Q²−R² with R=H²/sqrt(24). In d≥3 Q+R and Q−R are distinct irreducible real quadratics: each has at least two positive directions, no real-linear factorization. UFD reduces any competing decomposition to reciprocal factor scaling, and nonzero scalar Q plus rank-one R has rank at least d−1≥2, forcing unit scaling; swapping yields an inadmissible negative rank-one R. R=0 follows from unique irreducible square root. Covariance and displacement recovery then follows. Explicit positive definite d=2 pairs with Q1,R1,Q2,R2 share T and M but differ genuinely. Exact SymPy certificate tests formulas/positivity and order-two insufficiency. Full-dimensional proof is analytic, not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The exact claim is a GLOBAL injectivity theorem for the Fourier autocorrelation jet of two unit-mass Gaussians with strictly Loewner-ordered unequal anisotropic covariances in dimensions at least three, plus an explicit sharp planar noninjectivity example. Actual published-finding corpus searches and paper-level implication comparisons found no equivalent or stronger statement. Javed gives forward scalar-variance-mixing kurtosis, Agostini gives raw-moment homoscedastic recovery, and Blomenhofer et al. give generic degree-six centered recovery, none asserting this inverse phaseless threshold. Residual risk of older autocorrelation/tensor decomposition work and one inaccessible full text is recorded; search absence alone is not novelty proof.
residual_risks: An older complete Gaussian autocorrelation or fourth-cumulant tensor classification might already establish an equivalent rank-one factorization and dimension threshold.
Full text of Loperfido (2014) could not be inspected; available abstract does not cover unequal covariances, but absence from abstract is insufficient for a definitive negative statement.
published-finding corpus is a semantic index, so failure to retrieve matching formulations cannot establish exhaustive uniqueness or priority.

value.rationale: Natural inverse question is how much low-frequency phaseless information identifies two anisotropic Gaussian packets, a structured deconvolution/phase-retrieval model. The complete theorem supplies exact global recovery under a substantive Loewner-order hypothesis, proves minimal derivative order, and identifies a surprising dimension boundary using an explicit noncongruent planar counterexample; these are not merely parameter substitutions of earlier isotropic d≥2 results. It offers a useful structural limit on finite-jet imaging, while deliberately not claiming noise stability or broader mixture recovery.
